admission.authority: direct user request to lift primes and semiprimes to nearby composite divisor-count layers and search for structure
admission.reason: Preserve the full local composite tau spectrum, classify factor-forcing target layers, and expose the exact squarefree 2^(k-1)r prime-layer encoder as a small-number research probe.

methods.name: local divisor-layer lift and factor-forcing spectrum probe
capabilities: classify target T as factor-forcing whenever tau(n) does not divide T
prove lambda_T(n)=p_min^(r-2) for squarefree n with k primes and T=2^(k-1)r, r odd prime
retain all nearby composite divisor-count layers instead of prematurely collapsing to a mode
measure information loss caused by modal compression
run finite exact small-number diagnostics with explicit large-N non-claim boundaries
methods.core_law: If gcd(a,n)=1 then tau(an)=tau(a)tau(n), so tau(n) not dividing T forces every exact lift multiplier to overlap n. For squarefree n with k distinct prime factors and T=2^(k-1)r with r an odd prime, the divisor-product factorization has exactly k factors and forces exponent pattern (r-1,1,...,1), hence the minimal lift is p_min^(r-2).
methods.hard_boundary: The theorem does not provide lambda_T(n) from N alone and exact tau of arbitrary large neighbors can itself require factorization. This is currently an opportunistic observer/research probe, not a claimed large-integer factoring shortcut. Fixed small-layer frequencies are finite diagnostics and must not be extrapolated to RSA scale.
